title: The 12 Best Action RPGs
description: The 12 best action RPGs to play in 2026, ranked for combat, progression, build variety and exploration, from Elden Ring and Bloodborne to Cyberpunk 2077.
body:
Action RPG is a broad label, but the strongest games in the category share one idea: character growth matters because the player has to express that growth in real time. Better equipment, new abilities, and stronger builds only become interesting when movement, timing, positioning, and combat decisions make those systems visible.\n\nNeural Critic’s ranking favors action RPGs where combat and progression strengthen each other rather than games that simply attach a skill tree to an action adventure.

For deeper coverage of the top-ranked game, read our [Elden Ring review](/stories/elden-ring-review-monumental-open-world/) and [Elden Ring beginner’s guide](/stories/elden-ring-beginners-guide/).
author: Rouane Mounssif
imageAlt: Neural Critic feature illustration for The 12 Best Action RPGs.

contentBlocks.text: Diablo IV remains one of the clearest examples of the loot-driven action RPG. Skills, gear interactions, class identity, and increasingly specialized builds give combat a strong sense of forward motion. Its live structure will keep changing around the edges, but the core appeal is straightforward: every session gives the player another opportunity to make a character more efficient and expressive.
contentBlocks.caption: Diablo IV ranks No. 12 for its fast loot-driven progression and increasingly specialized character builds.
contentBlocks.heading: Diablo IV
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Image from Diablo IV accompanying its No. 12 entry in Neural Critic’s best action RPGs ranking.
contentBlocks.subtitle: Fast combat built around the pleasure of refining a build

contentBlocks.text: Dragon’s Dogma 2 is at its best when a journey goes wrong in an interesting way. Vocations create distinct combat roles, Pawns shape the party around the player, and large enemies turn terrain and positioning into part of the fight. Its friction is deliberate, sometimes excessively so, but few action RPGs make travel, combat, and character growth feel this physically connected.
contentBlocks.caption: Dragon’s Dogma 2 ranks No. 11 for tying party composition, exploration and large-scale encounters into one physical adventure.
contentBlocks.heading: Dragon’s Dogma 2
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Image from Dragon’s Dogma 2 accompanying its No. 11 entry in Neural Critic’s best action RPGs ranking.
contentBlocks.subtitle: Party-based exploration where preparation matters as much as execution

contentBlocks.text: Black Myth: Wukong places much of its weight on direct combat, but its transformations, spells, equipment, and skill choices give the player enough room to shape how those fights unfold. The result sits closer to an action game than some entries here, yet progression remains substantial enough to make preparation and build decisions matter alongside execution.
contentBlocks.caption: Black Myth: Wukong ranks No. 10 for pairing boss-focused action with spells, transformations and meaningful character progression.
contentBlocks.heading: Black Myth: Wukong
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Image from Black Myth: Wukong accompanying its No. 10 entry in Neural Critic’s best action RPGs ranking.
contentBlocks.subtitle: Boss-focused action supported by meaningful progression

contentBlocks.text: Monster Hunter Wilds treats weapon knowledge as a form of long-term progression. Gear matters, but so does learning a moveset deeply enough to recognize when to attack, reposition, or commit to a longer animation. Hunts create a satisfying loop of preparation, execution, and crafting that makes the next encounter feel easier because both the character and the player have improved.
contentBlocks.caption: Monster Hunter Wilds ranks No. 9 because weapon mastery, preparation and crafting make every successful hunt feed the next one.
contentBlocks.heading: Monster Hunter Wilds
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Image from Monster Hunter Wilds accompanying its No. 9 entry in Neural Critic’s best action RPGs ranking.
contentBlocks.subtitle: An action RPG where mastering a weapon is character progression

contentBlocks.text: Nioh 3 extends Team Ninja’s action-RPG identity around weapon mastery, timing, and build construction. Its combat asks more from the player than most games on this list, but that density is exactly what makes experimentation rewarding. Players who enjoy learning systems rather than simply raising damage numbers will find one of the genre’s deepest modern combat sandboxes.
contentBlocks.caption: Nioh 3 ranks No. 8 for deep action-RPG systems built around Samurai and Ninja styles, exploration and mechanical mastery.
contentBlocks.heading: Nioh 3
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Image from Nioh 3 accompanying its No. 8 entry in Neural Critic’s best action RPGs ranking.
contentBlocks.subtitle: A demanding combat system built for mechanical experimentation

contentBlocks.text: Dark Souls III compresses many of the series’ strengths into a faster and more directed adventure. Weapons and builds remain varied, but bosses are where the game’s identity becomes clearest: timing, spacing, stamina, and pattern recognition are constantly tested. It lacks Elden Ring’s freedom, but its concentration gives the campaign a distinctive momentum.
contentBlocks.caption: Dark Souls III ranks No. 7 for focused progression and a concentrated sequence of FromSoftware combat challenges.
contentBlocks.heading: Dark Souls III
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Image from Dark Souls III accompanying its No. 7 entry in Neural Critic’s best action RPGs ranking.
contentBlocks.subtitle: FromSoftware’s most focused Dark Souls combat

contentBlocks.text: NieR: Automata combines fluid combat with chips, weapons, levels, and customization, but its real strength is how willing it is to change perspective and structure around the player. The RPG systems are accessible rather than overwhelmingly deep, which lets the action support a much larger narrative experiment without getting in the way.
contentBlocks.caption: NieR: Automata ranks No. 6 for using accessible RPG progression to support a constantly changing action and narrative structure.
contentBlocks.heading: NieR: Automata
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Image from NieR: Automata accompanying its No. 6 entry in Neural Critic’s best action RPGs ranking.
contentBlocks.subtitle: Action-RPG systems serving a game that keeps changing form

contentBlocks.text: Hades turns repeated runs into both mechanical and narrative progression. Boons reshape a build from attempt to attempt, permanent upgrades gradually widen the player’s options, and conversations make returning to the hub feel like part of the reward. It is a roguelike first, but the way character growth and story accumulate gives it a strong place in the action-RPG conversation.
contentBlocks.caption: Hades ranks No. 5 because temporary run builds and permanent progression keep action and character growth moving together.
contentBlocks.heading: Hades
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Image from Hades accompanying its No. 5 entry in Neural Critic’s best action RPGs ranking.
contentBlocks.subtitle: A run-based action RPG where failure still builds momentum

contentBlocks.text: Cyberpunk 2077’s rebuilt progression model gives weapons, cyberware, attributes, and perks a clearer relationship than they had at launch. A stealth-focused netrunner and an aggressive close-range build can approach the same space very differently, while Night City gives those choices an unusually dense setting. Its strongest modern form finally lets build identity match the ambition of the world.
contentBlocks.caption: Cyberpunk 2077 ranks No. 4 for the way cyberware, attributes and perks now create sharply different approaches to Night City.
contentBlocks.heading: Cyberpunk 2077
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Image from Cyberpunk 2077 accompanying its No. 4 entry in Neural Critic’s best action RPGs ranking.
contentBlocks.subtitle: A flexible first-person RPG with a much stronger modern progression system

contentBlocks.text: The Witcher 3 remains important because combat is only one part of its role-playing. Signs, alchemy, equipment, preparation and character skills support a world where quests and consequences carry much of the emotional weight. In the current pre-Remastered build, its fighting is less precise than the games above it, but the combination of progression, exploration and authored storytelling remains difficult to match.\n\nCD PROJEKT RED launches The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Remastered on September 29, 2026 with an overhauled skill tree and improved combat, so Neural Critic will revisit this placement after the new version is available.
contentBlocks.caption: The Witcher 3 ranks No. 3 for combining action-RPG progression with some of the genre’s strongest quest writing and worldbuilding.
contentBlocks.heading: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Image from The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt accompanying its No. 3 entry in Neural Critic’s best action RPGs ranking.
contentBlocks.subtitle: Quest writing and role-playing weight inside an action-RPG structure

contentBlocks.text: Bloodborne takes familiar FromSoftware ideas and changes their rhythm. Regain rewards immediate counter-pressure, firearms reshape defensive timing, and trick weapons give individual movesets enormous personality. Character builds still matter, but the game’s greatest achievement is making aggression feel like a strategic decision rather than simply a faster way to play.
contentBlocks.caption: Bloodborne ranks No. 2 for turning aggression, recovery and distinctive weapon movesets into a singular FromSoftware combat identity.
contentBlocks.heading: Bloodborne
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Image from Bloodborne accompanying its No. 2 entry in Neural Critic’s best action RPGs ranking.
contentBlocks.subtitle: Aggressive combat transforms the Souls formula

contentBlocks.text: Elden Ring takes the top spot because its combat and progression are inseparable from exploration. A new weapon, spell, Spirit Ash, talisman, or route can completely change how a difficult encounter feels. The world gives players enough freedom to leave, experiment, rebuild, and return stronger, turning character progression into part of the act of discovery itself.
contentBlocks.caption: Elden Ring ranks No. 1 because exploration, build freedom and real-time combat continually change how the player approaches difficulty.
contentBlocks.heading: Elden Ring
contentBlocks.imageAlt: Image from Elden Ring accompanying its No. 1 entry in Neural Critic’s best action RPGs ranking.
contentBlocks.subtitle: The strongest combination of action, builds, and exploration

quickRead: Elden Ring ranks first for combining real-time combat, build freedom and open-ended exploration.
Bloodborne places second for its aggressive combat identity, while The Witcher 3 remains third for quest-driven role-playing.
Nioh 3, Monster Hunter Wilds, Cyberpunk 2077 and Hades show how broad the action-RPG category has become.
conclusion: The best action RPGs make progression visible in the player’s hands. A stronger build should change decisions, movement, timing, preparation, or the way a space is approached. Elden Ring does this across an enormous world, while Bloodborne proves how much identity can come from a tightly defined combat philosophy.\n\nBecause the category is so broad, Neural Critic’s ranking will continue to judge action RPGs by the relationship between systems and execution rather than by one narrow genre template.
conclusionHeading: Progression matters most when it changes how you play
